blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: GPU — Processor designed for highly parallel workloads.
multicore — CPU containing multiple execution cores.
data parallelism — Apply the same operation to many independent data elements.
bandwidth — Volume of data transferred in a given time.
synchronisation — Coordinating shared work and results.

blocks.title: GPUs and data parallelism
blocks.text: A GPU contains many execution resources suited to repeating similar calculations across graphics pixels or machine-learning tensors.

blocks.title: Multicore CPUs
blocks.text: Multiple CPU cores can run independent threads/processes, enabling greater throughput when tasks can be parallelised.

blocks.title: Evaluate overhead
blocks.text: Data transfers, branching, synchronisation and sequential tasks can reduce the ideal speedup. A GPU is not automatically best for every problem.

blocks.title: Worked example · Predict first
blocks.text: Divide 12 independent equal-sized tiles among four available cores.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain and check
blocks.text: Each core processes three tiles, so ideal completion is around one quarter of serial time only if work and overhead allow.
